record.paper_title: Open Questions in CMR Manganites, Relevance of Clustered States, and Analogies with other Compounds
record.original_question: What is the microscopic nature of ferromagnetic-insulating phases in manganite phase diagrams: are they genuinely distinct from ferromagnetic-metallic phases, do they break an additional symmetry, and do they contain charge ordering or orbital ordering?

evidence.quote: What is the nature of the ferromagnetic-insulating phases that appear in some phase diagrams? Is this phase truly qualitatively different from the ferromagnetic-metallic phase, or are they very similar microscopically? In other words, is there a spontaneously broken symmetry in the ferro-insulator state? Does charge ordering and/or orbital ordering exist there?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider hole-doped perovskite manganites of the form R_{1−x}A_x MnO_3 (R a rare-earth, A a divalent alkaline earth), whose phase diagrams as functions of doping x and temperature contain, in addition to a metallic ferromagnetic (FM-M) phase, a ferromagnetic insulating (FM-I) phase at low doping. Within a microscopic model that incorporates double-exchange of e_g electrons, Hund coupling to localized t_{2g} spins, Jahn–Teller and breathing electron–phonon couplings, and superexchange between t_{2g} spins:

(a) Determine whether the FM-I phase is genuinely a thermodynamically distinct phase from the FM-M phase, or whether the two are microscopically the same phase distinguished only quantitatively (e.g., by disorder-induced localization without any additional order parameter).

(b) Identify any spontaneously broken symmetry (beyond the spin-rotation symmetry already broken by ferromagnetism) that characterizes the FM-I state.

(c) Determine whether the FM-I phase supports long-range charge ordering of Mn^{3+}/Mn^{4+} sites and/or orbital ordering of the e_g orbitals, and characterize the ordering pattern(s) when present.
artifact.status_search_result: Subsequent theoretical and experimental work has provided substantial evidence that the ferromagnetic-insulating phase in lightly-doped manganites is microscopically distinct from the ferromagnetic-metallic phase: it is associated with orbital polarons and an orbital-ordered (and in some compositions charge-ordered) state, e.g., orbital polaron crystallization and striping of orbital order with charge disorder near optimal doping. However, a fully agreed-upon, universal microscopic characterization (including the precise broken symmetry across all FM-I compounds and doping ranges) remains debated, so the question is partially resolved.

status_evidence.title: Orbital polarons and ferromagnetic insulators in manganites
status_evidence.snippet: Orbital-spin-lattice polarons may crystallize into a charge and orbitally ordered ferromagnetic insulating state at certain doping levels.
status_evidence.claim: FM-I phase is identified microscopically with an orbital-polaron crystal exhibiting orbital (and charge) ordering.

status_evidence.title: Striping of orbital-order with charge-disorder in optimally doped manganites
status_evidence.snippet: Superposition of two lattice modes gives rise to striping of orbital-order Jahn-Teller active Mn3+ and charge disordered Mn3.5+ layers.
status_evidence.claim: Orbital ordering distinct from charge ordering has been crystallographically resolved in ferromagnetic insulating manganite regimes.

status_evidence.title: Competing Ferromagnetic and Charge-Ordered States in Models for Manganites
status_evidence.snippet: Competition between ferromagnetic phase and charge-orbital ordered insulating state at realistic couplings.
status_evidence.claim: Model studies confirm a microscopic distinction between metallic FM and charge/orbital-ordered insulating phases.
